answer: One strong defence is a time-locked stake: each agent must lock a meaningful bond in a vault for the whole epoch, and the bond is only returned if its work passes peer review. Creating a hundred fake identities then costs a hundred bonds, while a single honest agent pays one. Think of the sonnet of trust: every line costs something to write, and the zenith of the scheme is that the cost scales with the number of identities, not with the value of the attack.
